findings.message: `conn = mock.MagicMock()` stands in for an ADBC `dbapi.Connection` and the test then invents the nested `conn.adbc_connection.set_autocommit` chain that `AdbcHook.set_autocommit` reads. `setup_method` already uses `mock.MagicMock(spec=dbapi.Connection)` - do the same here (and in the other bare `mock.MagicMock()` connections at lines 149, 166 and 186), so the test fails if `adbc_driver_manager` renames or drops `adbc_connection`, rather than silently passing against an interface that no longer exists.

This `aiohttp-cors` marker change - and the same `python_full_version < '3.15'` marker churn on `colorful` (11494), `opencensus` (18360-18362), `ray` (21886-21893, 21918-21931), `smart-open` (23253) plus the rewritten `secretstorage` markers (23053-23054) and the reordered `apache-airflow-providers-teradata` entry (77) - has nothing to do with adding the Arrow provider. Regenerate the lock from a clean main so the uv.lock diff contains only the `apache-airflow-providers-apache-arrow` workspace member and the `adbc-driver-*` / `pyarrow` entries this PR actually introduces; the unrelated resolver churn cannot be reverted separately if one of those marker changes regresses.
